evidence: Plin. NH 33.103; Col. 12.3: praesēpia mundanda cūrāre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: post-Augustan, and later the word of Church Latin for cleansing; pūrgāre is the classical word.

phrases.english: to have the kitchen cleaned out

phrases.latin: Fenestrās tergeāmus: vix quicquam per eās cernitur.
phrases.english: Let’s clean the windows: you can hardly see a thing through them.
Today I’ll clean the bathroom and the toilet.

phrases.latin: hospite ventūrō cessābit nēmo tuōrum. ‘verre pavīmentum, nitidās ostende columnās, ārida cum tōtā dēscendat arānea tēlā.’
phrases.english: When a guest is coming, none of your household will sit idle. ‘Sweep the floor, make the columns shine, let every dry spider come down with all its web.’

sources: Lewis & Short: purgo · Lewis & Short: tergeo
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. clean house, clean up, tidy up, broom: dustpan, garbage, trash, garbage can, waste basket.
